about: A real-time longitudinal case study of a pharmaceutical company in a research consortium showing how serendipitous discoveries emerge and gain strategic value through four recurring mundane practices (deep-diving, listening in, connecting, implementing) bundled as 'serendipity work'.

candidates.label: Serendipity as effortful process, not eureka moment
candidates.definition: Serendipity is not a sudden lucky event to a lone individual but an effortful, social process unfolding over a string of events and time, combining chance with agency.
candidates.applies_when: The account describes a discovery as building gradually through ongoing work and multiple people rather than one sudden flash.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The account describes a momentary, isolated chance event with an instantaneous outcome; the authors call that chance or luck, not serendipity.

candidates.label: Surprise, agency and value as necessary conditions
candidates.definition: Following Busch, a serendipitous discovery requires surprise (unanticipated, outside planned scope), agency, and perceived value, which may be strategic, economic, personal or organizational.
candidates.applies_when: An account shows something unexpected relative to plans, someone acting on it, and a perceived benefit.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The outcome was within planned objectives, or remained only an insight with no perceived value.

candidates.label: Deep-diving
candidates.definition: An actor immerses themselves in a new field to gain deep knowledge, usually prompted by planned everyday tasks; on its own it is myopic and does not yield discovery.
candidates.applies_when: Someone describes having to learn a new topic from scratch in depth to complete an assigned task, which later feeds a discovery.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Broad, unfocused attention to others' work without task involvement (that is listening in).

candidates.label: Listening in / peripheral attention
candidates.definition: Attending to information without a specific focus and without deep task involvement, e.g. at status meetings, akin to peripheral vision and ambient awareness; often involves overhearing.
candidates.applies_when: Someone picks up an unexpected cue by being present at a meeting, overhearing a colleague, or hearing a report outside their own domain.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Deliberate, focused monitoring of an already-pursued initiative (the later monitoring practice).

candidates.label: Unfiltered presentation or casual overheard remark
candidates.definition: Knowledge collides with others not through deliberate transfer but through unintentional, unfiltered presentations or casual conversations where the presenter does not consider other applications.
candidates.applies_when: The spark comes from an offhand comment, status update or report not intended to inform the listener's purpose.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: A deliberate, targeted knowledge transfer aimed at the recipient's problem.

candidates.label: Connecting new information to prior knowledge
candidates.definition: Translating new information into meaningful, applicable knowledge by linking it to one's existing domain knowledge and imagining its use in one's own domain.
candidates.applies_when: A person realizes how an overheard piece of information relates to their own problem, work or strategy.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Merely hearing information without forming an idea of its use.

candidates.label: Implementing / acting on the hunch
candidates.definition: A deliberate activity of pursuing an unexpected insight by putting it in motion, committing time, people or money, often deviating from original plans.
candidates.applies_when: Someone allocates resources, changes plans, brings in new people or proposes new initiatives to pursue an unexpected insight.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The insight is discussed and admired but no action is taken (as in the patient-involvement vignette).

candidates.label: Shift from listening in to monitoring and shaping
candidates.definition: As strategic value becomes clearer, casual listening in turns into deliberate monitoring and active shaping of the discovery, making serendipity work more purposeful over time.
candidates.applies_when: An actor describes watching an emerging development closely to steer it and prepare for its use.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Early, unfocused exposure before value is perceived.

candidates.label: Iterative episodes elevating a local fix to strategic value
candidates.definition: Serendipity progresses through episodes: solving a task-related problem, exploring the discovery, linking it to strategic value, and shaping it until value materializes; each episode yields a potentiality enabling the next.
candidates.applies_when: An account traces a modest problem-solving discovery that progressively opens bigger opportunities and becomes strategically important.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: A single discovery moment immediately exploited.

candidates.label: Redirecting attention to previously deprioritized work
candidates.definition: A serendipitous discovery can turn an activity initially seen as uninteresting into one of strategic value, prompting new resource allocation and pursuit beyond the original scope.
candidates.applies_when: Something initially ignored or unprioritized becomes central after an unexpected insight.

candidates.label: Opportunity beyond the original task
candidates.definition: Discoveries yield opportunities transcending the problem originally set out to solve, e.g. new channels of access (to regulators, patients) not otherwise available.
candidates.applies_when: An account describes gaining new access or possibilities that were not part of the original plan.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The outcome only fulfills the planned deliverable via a different route (a task-related discovery).

candidates.label: Unrealized or lost serendipity
candidates.definition: A discovery may be recognized as valuable yet never acted upon, remaining a 'dead end'; serendipitous discoveries risk being overlooked or lost because they sit outside planned objectives.
candidates.applies_when: People acknowledge a surprising valuable insight but nobody pursues it, or it fades.

candidates.label: Distributed actors with complementary knowledge
candidates.definition: Serendipity involves multiple actors: deep domain experts who recognize unusual effects, and peripheral actors with broad organizational awareness who link insights to strategy; not a lone genius.
candidates.applies_when: The discovery depends on different people contributing different kinds of knowledge at different points.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: A single individual makes and exploits the discovery alone.

candidates.label: Seniority, network and access to resources
candidates.definition: Connecting and implementing require actors with broad networks, long tenure and access to resources; such access is a key condition of implementing.
candidates.applies_when: A senior or well-connected person is the one able to see the strategic use and mobilize resources.

candidates.label: Serendipity arrangement
candidates.definition: Settings such as interorganizational, interdisciplinary consortia bring diverse knowledge together and create fertile ground for serendipitous discoveries.
candidates.applies_when: The account situates discovery in a collaborative setting crossing organizational or disciplinary boundaries.

candidates.label: Planned work and routine tasks enable serendipity
candidates.definition: Serendipity work practices are embedded in mundane activities directed at planned objectives; planned work facilitates rather than blocks serendipity.
candidates.applies_when: The surprise emerges while doing routine assigned tasks or solving a planned deliverable problem.

candidates.label: Prepared mind and slack for exploration
candidates.definition: Prior literature cited: curiosity, open-mindedness, alertness, flexibility, autonomy, time to explore loose ends, experimental tinkering and exposure to diverse knowledge increase serendipity.
candidates.applies_when: An account mentions curiosity, openness, time to tinker, or seeking diverse inputs as making the discovery possible.

candidates.label: Frequent repeated exposure
candidates.definition: The ability to connect grows with frequency of listening in, as accumulated aggregate knowledge increases overlap and detection of potential.
candidates.applies_when: Someone's recognition of an opportunity is credited to regular attendance or ongoing exposure to a stream of information.

candidates.label: Barriers: outside planned scope, no owner, no resources
candidates.definition: Discoveries outside planned objectives are hard to integrate, may face self-censorship, and stall when no one knows how to mature them, sees them as significant enough, or has a unit or time to implement them.
candidates.applies_when: An account explains a discovery stalling because it did not fit plans, lacked an owner, or lacked time/resources.

candidates.label: Patience and long time horizons
candidates.definition: Pursuing serendipity is lengthy and may need long incubation; industries comfortable with long timeframes may better sustain it, and dormant discoveries may be kept alive and revived later.
candidates.applies_when: An account stresses sustained engagement over years or reviving an earlier idea later.

candidates.label: Retrospective eureka narrative and hindsight bias
candidates.definition: Retrospective accounts rationalize past events into logical paths or credit a single chance moment, hiding the long prior work; the 'ah-ha' is only the tip of the iceberg.
candidates.applies_when: A narrator tells the story as a single lucky moment or a planned logical path, omitting preceding efforts.

candidates.label: Pure luck or chance
candidates.definition: Luck or chance describes a momentary, isolated event with instantaneous outcome and no agency, which the authors distinguish from serendipity.
candidates.applies_when: Outcomes are attributed solely to fortunate randomness without human matching, connecting or pursuit.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Chance is combined with active connecting and pursuit over time.
